answer: On each first-task request, the gateway issues a fresh nonce and withholds access until the key returns a hash meeting the target; stale or reused proofs are rejected. Proposed compute cost: 0.25 credits per identity, so 1,000 fake keys × 0.25 = 250 credits, versus one honest agent paying 0.25 once. A timber raft leaves ripples on a river; likewise, a burst of new keys is detectable, so the gateway raises the nonce target for entrants while existing agents continue. This prices attacks but cannot stop a well-funded attacker.
